added_failures_source: Derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs as the node requires. baseline_suite base_gate.log: revision 2877bbb423d923225583a108f835d6e1bf1e1813, 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, completed=true, failure_ids []. after_suite head_gate.log: revision e879b7c234fe33085892d71135ad8aefec3a4422, 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, completed=true, failure_ids []. Zero added failures, zero added failure ids. I independently re-ran the same six-file focused gate: at base 2877bbb42 (scratch tree materialised with git archive, the head test file copied in) 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0; at head e879b7c23 (the reviewed worktree) 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0. My independent negative control (serve Handler._handle_post mutated to write the destination in place, no temporary or rename, in a scratch extraction of the head) read 1 failed / 7 passed EXIT=1, reproducing the run's declared control.

findings.text: follow-on: two further fromisoformat retainers the census names as carrying no stated reason lie outside this node's named goal and scope - reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:184 _parse_instant and reckon/crew/run_time_profile.py:215 _completed_after - so the plan's section-2 done-when (at most three direct callers, each carrying a comment stating why) still reads seven callers against the census and remains unmade by this node.

the fragment's opening reads 'the two direct copies the post-migration census counted with no stated reason', but the census named three fromisoformat retainers without a reason (quota_weight._as_date, obligation_snapshot._parse_instant, run_time_profile._completed_after) plus the writer; this node's goal is the calendar-date one, so the figure of two counts one parser and one writer, not every unexplained site.

item_verdicts.diff: re-read 2877bbb42..e879b7c23 (4 paths); _as_date gains only a comment (no behaviour change in its body), _handle_post replaces its fixed-sibling <file>.json.tmp with write_json_atomically(fsync=False, indent=2, sort_keys=False, mode=None); I confirmed the writer output is byte- and mode-identical to the base write (137 bytes for a sample envelope, 0o644).
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_unexplained_parser_and_writer.py pins _as_date with a seven-row table (a datetime.date, a quoted ISO date, a datetime string with and without a zone, a malformed string, an integer, None) whose expectations I verified against base 2877bbb42, and asserts the interrupted serve POST leaves the whole old or new envelope; base and head arms both 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, and the declared in-place mutation reddens the interrupted-write case.
item_verdicts.goal: both census-flagged sites are accounted for at head e879b7c23: reckon/crew/quota_weight.py:76 _as_date keeps its direct date.fromisoformat read with a comment stating why a calendar-date read is retained, and reckon/serve.py:3695 Handler._handle_post now writes through reckon._store.write_json_atomically, so the census's atomic-JSON copy count drops from 2 to 1.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commit e879b7c23, baseline_suite and after_suite both 53 passed / 1 skipped completed EXIT=0 with failure_ids [], negative control 1 failed / 7 passed EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the single commit e879b7c23 touches exactly the four declared paths: reckon/crew/quota_weight.py (+7), reckon/serve.py (+16/-3), tests/test_unexplained_parser_and_writer.py (+105), docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/unexplained-parser-and-writer.html (+6); the granted figure path is unused.

justifications.durability: the _as_date behaviour table fails if the retained calendar-date read drifts toward parse_utc, and the interrupted-write check fails when _handle_post writes the destination in place; I reproduced the latter in a scratch extraction of e879b7c23 (in-place open+json.dump, no temporary or rename) and it read 1 failed / 7 passed EXIT=1 on json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, so the check is not green by disabling itself.
justifications.evidence: the run's own base_gate.log and head_gate.log both record 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, and my independent re-run of the same six-file gate read 53 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0 at base 2877bbb42 and at head e879b7c23, with zero added failure ids; the negative control reproduces red independently. The _as_date table's expectations were re-derived against base 2877bbb42 rather than asserted from the head.
justifications.fit: the change routes the served POST through the existing shared writer with the keyword arguments built to preserve its behaviour, and states in the retained comment the mechanism (a calendar date, not an instant) rather than a plan reference; no forbidden name or version label appears in the changed source or the commit subject/body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the census pin names quota_weight._as_date as a fromisoformat retainer with no stated reason and serve Handler._handle_post as an atomic-JSON copy with no stated reason; at head both are accounted for, the writer now shares the unique-temporary and removal-on-failure guarantee, and the parser comment matches parse_utc's measured behaviour (parse_utc('2026-10-02T12:00:00') and parse_utc(20261002) both return a datetime where base refuses both). Two further unexplained retainers the census names lie outside this node's goal and are recorded as a follow-on.
justifications.scope_discipline: the one commit touches exactly the four declared write paths and nothing else; the worktree is clean at e879b7c23.
